content.short: Filecoin is a decentralized storage network for humanity to perpetually keep data.
content.description: Filecoin organizes its network around three main roles: builders who create applications and services on the network, storage providers who offer capacity, and users who pay to store data. The Filecoin protocol itself does not control or manage the stored content; it provides a distributed system for data storage governed by the network’s rules. In this model, participants pay to store data, and the owners or operators of storage nodes receive fees in exchange for delivering the storage service. This arrangement distributes data storage across a network of storage providers.

resources.title: Filecoin's NV28 'Fire Horse' Network Upgrade
resources.tldr: Smart contracts can now verify the health, status and expiry of any storage sector onchain, part of a push toward paid storage deals and better economics.

resources.title: Filecoin's 2026 Shift Toward Paid Storage
resources.tldr: The strategy moves from how much data the network can hold to how much it is paid to store and serve, and what that asks of builders.

resources.title: Solstice: Reshaping How Storage Providers Earn
resources.tldr: A proposal to drop the special approval process for higher rewards, the largest change to Filecoin's reward system since launch.
